THREE READINGS, not settled by the strokes: (a) a person standing in the gate (structures_w's and mine, low); (b) a gathered cloth (the tile restyle paints a white cloth tied in a knot here; then it is part of S3.bld.tavern_gate_16870 and this entity is declined); (c) the overview restyle paints the lamp-box's east face wider here, as a white panel with characters, but the scan's 十千 face is at u 17052-17068, west of these strokes. That fits a man seated with his knees up, about 0.55-0.6 of the 152-160 px standing men at the door, so about 85-95 px from head to ground with the ground under him at v ~1650-1670; a standing man would leave the knee mass unexplained. entities.name: two-wheeled handcart pulled up the north bank
entities.what: Two-wheeled handcart on the north bank just north of the bridge's north ramp: a slatted box body with two long top rails that run on as shafts at its west end, one big spoked wheel showing on the near side under the body's east half. One man pulls it west by the shafts, a second leans on it at the wheel; no animal is harnessed. No load is drawn above the rails (the box may hold goods).
entities.vis: part: the far wheel and the shaft tips hidden by the puller
entities.note: Front = ground under the shaft tips at the west end, where the puller S3.fig.cart_puller_19870 holds them; rear = ground under the box's east end (about 19975). Which end is the front is read from the puller leaning west with his feet east of his head; if the cart is being backed east, front and rear swap (both ends are in t9's range either way). SCALE CUE: wheel about 78 px tall (v 142-220), so about 1 m; box about 95 px long (19880-19975), side about 40 px high (v 158-198). The top rails run (19862,140) -> (19975,123), slope dv/du -0.15 (raised rails, not a ground edge). A thin pole runs on north-east from the rails' east end to about (20021, 115): a third shaft or a prop stick. East of the wheel is a dark lumpy mass (S3.tree.shrub_or_heap_20025), which the overview restyle paints as foliage; if it is the cart's covered load instead, the cart's rear moves to about 20055. A pale crouching shape at 19790-19845, v 160-215 just west of the puller (a dog, or a figure crouching) is t8's by its u and may belong to this group.

entities.name: boat moored along the south bank

Two men stand and lie on the roof waving and shouting to the big boat (上下呼救). The dark-trunk tree (t9's) crosses in front of it at u 20380-20460. No mast, sweep or crew working it.
entities.vis: part: the shops' roofs hide the hull below v ~1150-1170; the dark-trunk tree and a parasol (t8's) cross it
entities.src: 余辉: 上下呼救 (setting)
entities.note: SEAM: S3's whole (area brief), though its east end (~20630) lies past u 20500: the lead tells S2. The restyle paints it as house roofs; the scan shows a boat's arched mat roof, a hatch, a long low roof and a hull side with an arched opening, with the men standing on it. ORIENTATION unknown (conf low): front is put at the west end, where the coiled ropes lie (a bow's gear); the other reading turns it by 180 (front (20640, 1195), facing 0). Both ends are est: the hull's lower edge is behind the shops' roofs (t8 reads it at v ~1165-1185), so the waterline is est at v ~1185-1190; the west end slopes down at u 19720-19745, v 1100-1162. SCALE CUE: about 895 px long (19742-20637); roof top v ~1085 over the waterline est v ~1188 (about 100 px); the standing waver is 155 px tall (foot v 1097), the reclining one's head 30 px across.

entities.name: big boat lowering its mast (大船抢险)
entities.what: The big cargo boat at the bridge, lying crosswise with its squared bow to the west-south-west and its high stern against the north bank: an open forward deck with a windlass and rope drum at the bow (u 19550-19610, v 700-735) and a long striated bundle (the lowered mat sail or coiled cables) over the forward deck (u 19630-19790, v 575-615); a low mat-roofed deckhouse amidships (u 19920-20060, v 575-640) with men under it; a planked after cabin with an open door on its south side (u 20050-20330, v 450-650); a high stern deck (u 20150-20400, v 300-395) and a high stern with its rudder (blade in the water at u 20400-20470, v 560-600). Its A-frame mast is being lowered aft: the legs lie diagonally from the foot amidships (hidden) to the head at (20295, 175), lashed with bindings near the top, with its lines hanging in loose curves down onto the after deck, where the stern crew haul them. Four or five long poles slant from the near-side crew into the water off the south side (lower ends at u ~19730-19990, v 790-810); two crewmen push poles up toward the arch and the cabin boat under it; a long pole held by the man in the cabin door reaches east past the stern to about (20600, 548). A rope thrown from the bridge's crown railing by S3.fig.deck_youth_rope_19445 (t8; the line leaves his hands at about (19471, 244)) hangs in a loop down to about (19600, 420) in front of the cabin boat's roof, toward the forward crew's raised hands; S3.fig.deck_pole_holder_19625 (t8) holds a long pole or taut rope level over the railing at the crown (19585-19658, v 209-228), its far end not painted; S3.prop.bundle_over_rail_19392 (t8) hangs over the railing, perhaps on a rope. Two U-shaped loops hang under the arch's rib at (19772, 392) and (19855, 390): rope loops round the rib or the bridge's iron hooks (conf low). Not rafted; under way, poled.
entities.vis: part: the crew, the rigging and the after cabin hide the far side; the stern's waterline is behind the rudder
entities.src: 名画记: 大船穿行虹桥 (pin 19); 余辉: 大船抢险, 上下呼救
entities.note: ORIENTATION: the west end is the bow (windlass with a rope drum, squared bow board, crew poling and reaching forward toward the bridge); the east end is the stern (rudder blade in the water, high stern deck, the mast lowered aft onto it). The setup's 'bow ≈ 20450' is the stern; both ends are inside S3 (u 19510-20480). HEADING: the near-side waterline runs (19700, 790) -> (20330, 645), slope -0.23, which in this frame (dx ~31.6) is about 22° north of east, so the bow points about 200° (west-south-west), i.e. the hull lies across the current, as 余辉's 大船抢险 tells. WATERLINE: near side along the hull band's lower edge (19518, 766) bow, (19600-19900, ~790), rising to (20100, 740) and (20330, 645) at the stern quarter; the far side is hidden (beam_n est from the far-side crew's feet at v ~595-605, which agree with a beam of about 4 m at 48 px of v per metre across the axis). FREEBOARD: near gunwale (19800, 732) over waterline (19800, 792) = 60 px; bow_top (19515, 700) over the stem's waterline (19518, 766) = 66 px. The stern crew stand on the poop, the high deck over the after cabin (floor v ~375-395 at u 20200-20360; support boat roof:); its height above water can't be read straight down (the stern's waterline is hidden behind the rudder): the cabin's south eave (20200, 470) over the near-side waterline (20200, 700) gives about 230 px, so about 2.5-3 m above water (est; the frame's choice). MAST: legs from about (19930, 560, est) to the head (20295, 175); the foot is hidden in the crowd of crew and ropes. SCALE CUE: hull 880 px along u from stem to sternpost; near-side hull band 60 px deep amidships; crew painted heights 73-120 px (bow men ~90 px with feet at v ~700; near-side polers 85-118 px at v ~720-740; stern crew ~73-95 px at v ~375-395). The restyle (tiles and overview) redraws this boat lower and further west and drops most of its crew: every point here is from the scan. SECOND PASS (east): a third hook or rope loop hangs under the arch's rib at (19973-20000, v 397-417), in line with the two U-shaped loops at (19772, 392) and (19855, 390) in this boat's what. It is the C-shaped stroke river_e recorded as head_in_rigging_19990 (retired at the second pass) (retire proposed). Crew count after the proposed retirements: 19 (was 21): head_in_rigging_19990 (retired at the second pass) and boatman_stern_rail_20400 (retired at the second pass) drop. Crops: p2e_c_loops_col.jpg, p2e_c_loops.jpg, p2e_c_nfoot_col.jpg, p2e_c_poop_plain.jpg.

entities.name: narrow empty skiff under the arch's south foot
entities.what: A long, narrow, empty skiff lying in the water under the south half of the arch, parallel to the south bank: a slim hull seen side-on, about 340 px long, its sharp west end running in behind the arch's south leg and its east end rising to an upturned stem with a small knob on its tip; four short uprights (frames or thwarts) stand between gunwale and bottom over its east half. No crew, oar, pole or mooring line is painted.
entities.vis: part: its west end runs in behind the arch's south leg (u ~18915-18935); the south-east end post crosses it at u ~19015
entities.note: SECOND PASS (middle): replaces floating_timber_19090 (retired at the second pass) (edit below: retire it). Strokes on contrast crops at zoom 3-4: gunwale (top line) (18933, 947) -> (19014, 964) -> (19100, 975) -> (19160, 975) -> (19252, 945); bottom (18933, 961) -> (19014, 983) -> (19100, 1000) -> (19160, 997) -> (19255, 967). The depth grows from ~14 px in the west to ~25 px at u 19100-19160, then both lines rise together into a stem whose tip carries a small knob at (19250-19260, 943-952), with a short post down to (19258, 965). Uprights between the lines at u 19108-19113, 19160-19170, 19185-19192 and 19210-19215 (v ~970-1000). This is a hull's profile: a log or spar keeps one depth along its length and has no rising stem. BOW: the upturned stem is east, so front = the waterline under it; the west end is sharp and hidden, rear est where the two lines meet behind the arch's leg. pose 'moored' is a reading: nothing ties it and nobody is in it; it lies ~40-60 px north of the south bank's est shore (v ~1040), under the ridge of S3.bld.mat_shed_19160. OTHER READINGS, kept: a long timber or spar afloat (river_e's first reading), or a footing timber of the bridge's south abutment (river_e); neither explains the stem with its knob. t7 and the bridge agent also read a skiff. OWNER: its main point (front, u 19255) falls in the east range; the merge listed it for the middle pass. SCALE CUE: hull ~340 px long (4.4 m at 77 px/m), ~20-25 px deep. Crops: scratchpad/S3_second_middle/i_timber.jpg, i_timber_e.jpg, i_timber_w.jpg, i_timber_m.jpg.

entities.name: cabin boat under the arch
entities.what: A long boat lying under the bridge's arch, behind (north of) the big boat: a planked hull side with a row of iron cramps (v 525-580), a cabin with a railed open side (posts at u ~19320, 19370, 19420, 19470, 19515, 19585, 19645, 19700; rail v 480-525) and a top beam at v ~445, under a planked roof that disappears behind the arch's rib. Two men lean on the railing looking out at the big boat. No mast, oars or poles show.
entities.vis: part: the arch's rib cuts its west end, the big boat's crew and rigging hide its east half, the bridge's deck hides its roof
entities.src: 名画记: 大船穿行虹桥 (pin 19) (setting)
entities.note: Found here, not in the setup's list (which had 3 boats for river_e). BOTH READINGS: (1) a separate cabin boat passing under the bridge: its hull band ends in the west at the arch's intrados (u ~19225-19290; a vertical joint at 19288, darker planks to 19230), it has its own waterline (v ~580, water with ripples below it at u 19200-19480) about 190 px north of the big boat's near-side waterline, and the big boat's bow (u 19518) lies south of it with water between (u 19480-19520, v 585-700); (2) the restyle (overview and tiles) paints the whole structure as the bridge's own underside framework. The planked surface above the cabin's top beam (v 330-445, boards slanting down to the south-east) may be its roof or the arch's underside beams; the railing with two men leaning on it, the hull's cramps and the waterline make the lower part a boat. Which way it heads is not painted (both ends hidden); front is put at the west end (est) by convention. SCALE CUE: hull at least 725 px (19225-19950), hull band 55 px deep (cabin floor v ~525 over waterline v ~580), railing posts 50-70 px apart; the two men 72-74 px from head to the cabin floor. SECOND PASS (east): the merge asked whether this is a boat or the bridge's underside framework, and it is a boat. On a colour crop at zoom 1.8 the hull band (19283-19650+, v 524-580) carries the same 工-shaped iron cramps as the other hulls. Ripples are drawn right under its lower edge, and two passengers lean on a railing of posts and rails (v 480-524). Above them a planked roof with rafters slopes up under the arch's rib (v 347-447). The hull's west end is a square vertical edge at u ~19283 just inside the rib. Two passengers only: the cabin east of 19470 is empty. Crops: p2e_c_cabinboat_col.jpg, p2e_c_cabinpax_col.jpg.

entities.name: 串车 heaped with a bound load
entities.what: 串车 (a barrow-type cart) standing in the open ground in front of the canopy, its huge domed load bound with ropes: a mass of looping, scribbled strokes under big arched hoops, vertical stakes at its west end and a ribbed woven panel (a rolled mat or a basket) at its north-east; two long poles stick out east from the load's top with loops of rope hanging from them, and two long handles run down west-south-west almost to the ground. Nothing draws it: no animal and no puller is painted at either end; two men work at its west (handle) end (t3's).
entities.vis: part: wheel and body hidden by the load; the men at the west end hide the handles' roots
entities.src: 名画记: 串车 (pin 24); 余辉: 书屏遭废 (its load a cursive-script screen used as a tarp)
entities.note: FRONT/REAR: front = east. The two long handles at the west end lie low (tips at about (17440, 1525) and (17455, 1545), only 20-30 px above the cart's ground line), as a barrow's handles do when it is set down, and the two men at that end (t3's: a capped man at head (17543, 1325) and a man with a topknot at head (17500, 1335)) face east and lean into the load. The east end has no shafts at ground level, only the load's poles at v 1320-1345 and hanging rope loops (u 17760-17790, down to v ≈ 1495, one ending in a hook). Reading B: the west poles are shafts and the cart faces west; then its front would be (17440, 1530) and it would be t3's. LOAD: 余辉 reads it as a cursive-script screen used as a tarp; the strokes show dense looping lines that could be cursive writing or a tangle of ropes and sticks (the restyle paints a tangle of timber). WHEEL: the big arcs (top v ≈ 1305 at u 17560-17700, east side to u ≈ 17770, lower rim v ≈ 1540-1550 at u 17590-17680) read as one big wheel about 240 px across, hub ≈ (17640, 1430), half hidden by the load (like S5.veh.cart_screen_8510's one big wheel); they could also be the hoops over the load, so the wheel contact is est. Two short dark uprights under the body at (17512, 1550) and (17605, 1562) are the barrow's rest legs, or the feet of a man hidden behind the load. SCALE CUES: load 320 px long (u 17470-17790) and 245 px high (v 1305-1550). DEPTH DIRECTION: none drawn; the cart is side-on (handle line (17560, 1490) -> (17440, 1525), slope -0.29, runs down to the west, not a receding edge). SEAM: the cart spans t3 and t4; t3's part agrees it is t4's (front east, handles resting on the ground at the west); t3's two men at its west end are S3.fig.topknot_man_at_cart_17458 and S3.fig.cap_man_at_cart_17545 (join them to S3.grp.chuanche_17775 at merge).

The lowered mast: 'mast' = the crutch's foot where the spar rests, 'mast_top' = the spar's east end; the festooned line at 18050-18300, v 220-245 (rope lashings or a furled sail) continues it over B6. SCALE CUE: ~290 px long; lowered spar ~370 px.

entities.name: boat unloading at the south bank
entities.what: A cargo boat moored along the south bank with its bow west toward the 新酒 pole: a short bow beam with a small hanging box (17650-17700, v 820-850), a multi-pronged grapnel anchor (4-5 hooked prongs) hanging under the bow (17700-17780, v 855-930) and a long pole or sweep running from the bow west-south-west over the water to ~(17480, 885); six men stand and bend on the foredeck (17700-17950, v 800-830) over jars and bundles (a jar at (17728, 770-800)); dark sacks or baskets heaped amidships (17900-17990, v 850-890); the stern half (17950-18250) is covered by an arched mat hood (18095-18200, v 735-800) and flat lattice mat awnings on poles (17960-18330, v 740-880; poles at ~18010 and ~18170).
entities.vis: part: the stern hidden by the mat awnings and t5's parasol (18050-18250, v 870-980)
entities.note: WATERLINE: the near-side hull bottom runs (17780, 850) -> (17870, 900) -> (18000, 925) -> (18050, 940), then under the parasol; the stern est. MATS: read as this boat's stern cover; other readings (the restyle and overview paint stalls): a second, mat-hooded boat moored astern of it (hull hidden), or a mat-awning stall on the bank (then t4's or t5's prop). Its hull ends where t5's parasol stall begins. SCALE CUE: waterline ~415 px; crew 110-135 px tall; bow beam ~45 px. The grapnel: prongs splay from (17740, 855) to tips at (17710, 915), (17730, 925), (17745, 915), (17760, 910), (17775, 895); other reading: a bundle of poles or oars hanging into the water. The long pole from the bow to ~(17480, 885) passes the 新酒 pole's crossed frame (t4's prop at 17605) without touching it. Second pass: the arched stern hood spans u 18095-18200 (its arch from (18093, 760) over (18150, 737) to (18202, 792); scratchpad/S3_second_middle/c_stern2.jpg, c_stern_plain.jpg), so the stern is under its east end: rear moved from (18120, 950, est), which lay under the hood's middle, to (18210, 958, est) on the hull line (17780, 850) -> (18050, 940) carried east under the big parasol. The flat lattice panel reaches (18327, 812-825). East of ~18190 that panel lies over the south ramp's west edge (the deck's far edge is ~720 px west of deck_e: 18190 at v 840), so its east part may be an awning of the stall at the ramp's edge (the tray stall) rather than the boat's; the boat ends at the deck's edge either way. Waterline length now ~505 px.

entities.name: boat with a fore awning and mat cabin, moored at the far bank
entities.what: A moored boat, bow west: a pointed bow under a mat awning on a light frame (17365-17510, v 230-300) with poles or oars lying across the foredeck and projecting west to ~17345 (v 300-340), a crouching boatman under the awning at 17420-17470 (S3.fig.awning_boatman_17435; low, or cargo); a large cabin with a high dark mat roof (17510-17760, v 205-240) with a crossed pole frame at its east end; a man sits inside at a window (S3.fig.passenger_seated_17632); bundles of cargo under the roof (17560-17720, v 240-280); two posts with small box lamps or plaques at the cabin's ends (17553, v 265-345, and 17700, v 275-370).
entities.vis: part: its east end hidden by the next boat and the post
entities.note: Bow west: the pointed prow and fore awning are at the west end. Its east end is hard to tell from the next boat B5 (the crossed frame at 17720-17770 may be either boat's: given to B5 as its mast crutch). SCALE CUE: waterline 17442-17705 ~265 px; cabin roof 250 px long, ~35 px deep. The bundle of poles at the bow (17345-17470, v 300-345) points at B3's stern platform (17250-17345, v 375-395): a gangplank between them is possible but not clear.

entities.name: long passenger boat moored at the far bank
entities.what: A very long passenger boat with a continuous cabin: at the west (bow) end a deckhouse with open windows (16400-16510, v 245-340), then a long cabin with lattice windows (16500-17060, roof v 245-300, windows v 310-360) with a raised roof section and skylight on top at 16640-16760, a short slanted pole above the roof at (17060-17080, v 225-265), and at the east end a raised upper deckhouse (17150-17330, v 250-300) over a stern cabin; a plank platform and a slanted post (rudder?) at the stern (17250-17345, v 360-395). Moored along the far bank, bow west.
entities.vis: part: the far side and the waterline at the ends hidden
entities.note: One hull: the near-side bottom line runs unbroken from (16395, 335) to (17300, 388). Bow west: pointed prow at 16385-16395 (v 300-340); the east end has the rudder post and stern platform. Brief's two far-bank boats '16380-16700' and '16600-17300' are this one boat. SCALE CUE: waterline length ~945 px; lattice window bays ~40-50 px wide; cabin height window sill to roof ~60 px. The slanted pole at 17060-17080 may be a stubbed or lowered mast (two thin poles in the restyle). The restyle fills the cabin with diners at 16540-16760; the scan shows at most one figure (see S3.fig.passenger_door_16553).

entities.name: masted boat towed by trackers
entities.what: A heavily laden boat with a tall mast (a ladder-like pole with cross cleats, or a bipod seen edge-on) and many stays fanning from the masthead to both ends; big mat-covered cargo heaped high over the bulging stern half (west); a towline runs from the masthead (16075, 45) east-north-east across the water to the rear tracker on the far-bank path (S3.fig.tracker_16333, t2's, at (16325, 112)). At the bow (east) a projecting beam (16170-16235, v 225-250) and a man poling with a long pole into the water (pole foot ~(16245, 308)).
entities.vis: full
entities.src: 名画记: 河边泊船 (纤夫) (pin 25)
entities.note: Bow east: the towline goes from the masthead to five trackers walking up the far bank to the east, and the projecting bow beam and the poler are at the east end. SCALE CUE: waterline length ~255 px; mast from deck (est v ~228) to top v 12 = ~215 px; hull painted depth gunwale-to-waterline ~70-90 px. WATERLINE: near side v ~330-335 at 16050-16150; ends est. The towline's far end is a tile figure (t2: S3.fig.tracker_16333 and four more trackers ahead of him to (16430, 48)).

entities.name: boat under way, sculled with a stern sweep (摇橹向前?)
entities.what: A mid-sized river boat with a big arched mat roof over most of its length (15610-15900, v 300-470; the restyle tiles it), a high rounded bow at the west end with a curved beam projecting west (15555-15600, v 275-290) and an A-frame of two poles at the bow; three men stand at the bow (on the raised foredeck) and five work a long sweep (橹) over the low stern at the east end: its loom runs from the crew past a pivot at (15965, 503) to a blade lying in the water at 16070-16135, v 555-570. Cargo under the roof (no figures painted inside). No mast up.
entities.vis: full
entities.src: 名画记: 河边泊船 (纤夫) (pin 25 at 15690); 余辉: 摇橹向前
entities.note: WHICH END IS THE BOW: read as bow west (facing ~162, moving west): the 橹 is a stern oar worked over the stern, and the west end carries the high rounded stem and the projecting beam that the towed boat B2 carries at its bow. Other reading: bow east with a bow sweep (Song river boats also steer with a bow sweep; S4b's big rafted boat has a sweep at its east end, which S4b reads as its bow): then front/rear swap and facing ~342. SCALE CUE: waterline length ~370 px along the hull (15595-15955), painted height bow top to waterline ~140 px; crew painted 60-90 px tall (bow men ~62 px, stern men ~80 px). WATERLINE: beam_s = the hull's lowest near-side outline (v 515-528 at 15700-15900); the ends est where the outline turns up (west end outline at 15578, v 380-420); beam_n hidden behind the roof (est from the far gunwale at the stern deck and the roof's far edge). Sweep blade 16070-16135 at v 555-570 lies on the water south-east of the stern.

entities.name: dark low mass east of the handcart (shrub or covered heap)
entities.what: A dark, mottled, lumpy mass about 65 px across on the north bank between the handcart's wheel and the bridge's north end post, with an irregular top: a low shrub, or a heap of goods under a cover.

Two readings: a shrub (the overview restyle paints green foliage here) or a heap of goods (or the cart's covered load, which would lengthen S3.veh.handcart_19862 to about 20055). No trunk shows. If a heap, it should be retired and recorded as a prop. SECOND PASS (east): not the handcart's load. On a colour crop at zoom 2.5 the mass (19988-20052, v 148-200) is stippled like massed leaves, and it lies east of and lower than the box's east end (the top rails end at about (19975-20000, 124-132)). So the cart keeps its rear at ~19978, and the shrub reading is preferred over a covered heap (conf stays low). Crop: p2e_c_northfoot_col.jpg.

entities.name: bare twiggy tree behind the deck's south end (the eastern of a pair)
entities.what: Bare tree with long thin straight twigs fanning upward from a short hidden trunk, beside the western one; no leaves. Medium size.

entities.name: willow crown behind the deck crowd (west of the pair)

entities.name: old willow on the far bank (leaning trunk)

entities.name: bare willow head behind the hall's roof (west)

entities.src: sections.md: 十千脚店 lamp-box ≈ 17000
entities.note: Box u 17003-17068, v 1550-1690 (crest v 1550-1578; front face u 17003-17052; side face u 17052-17068). Its bottom meets the fence's top rail at v ~1692, so it either stands on the ground behind the fence (foot est) or sits on the fence. SCALE: box 65 px wide, 140 px tall. Free-standing as painted, so recorded as a tile prop (t2 and the brief: "structures_w's unless it stands on its own"); if structures_w also writes it into the gate's what, keep this entry. Kept here as the tile prop; it is a member of the tavern group S3.grp.shiqian_jiaodian_16800.

entities.name: big round basin of fruit or flowers in front of the diners' table
entities.what: A large round, bowl-shaped vessel (a basin, or a woven basket) standing on the balcony floor in front of the dining table's east end, its belly hatched, heaped high with lumpy round things touched with pink and red (S3.prop.food_heap_16170): fruit, buns or flowers.
entities.vis: part: its foot behind the balcony's inner rail
entities.note: SECOND PASS (west): replaces diner_back_16180 (retired at the second pass) (reading (b) of that figure's own note; see edits). Strokes: the rounded outline u 16152-16208, v 1380-1413 is narrowest at the top, where the heap sits on it (v ~1380), and widens into a smooth convex belly at the bottom (v 1405-1413), with diagonal hatching inside: the shape of a bowl or a basket, not of a back. A seated back would be widest at the shoulders, at its top, and show a collar, a neck or hair under the heap; none is drawn, and the heap (58 x 38 px) is too big for a head (heads here are 18-25 px). The restyle paints a big blue-grey man here, like the woman in red and the extra diners it invents in this hall. Base est at the vessel's bottom; the floor line in front of the table is v ~1430 (S3.fig.diner_hunched_16050). About 55 px across (~0.7 m at the street's scale; a builder choice). Crops: c_heap.jpg, insp_heap.jpg, c_hall_m.jpg.

entities.name: heap of round food (or flowers) on the table
entities.what: A big heap of lumpy round things touched with pink and red, piled high in the round basin (S3.prop.basin_16180) that stands in front of the dining table's east end: fruit, buns or flowers.
entities.vis: full
entities.note: Mass u 16142-16200, v 1340-1378, about 58 x 38 px, with squiggly outlines and pink touches (red is rare on this silk). It could also be (a) the flowered head or patterned back of the diner seen from behind (diner_back_16180, retired at the second pass), or (b) the contents of a basin standing in front of the table (see that figure's note). The restyle paints a dark heap of cloth here. Second pass: the heap sits on the basin's rim (v ~1380), not on the table; its support follows the basin (diner_back_16180 retired). Readings (a) and (b) of the note above are settled as (b).

entities.name: long dining table in the balcony's middle bay
entities.what: A long low table across the balcony's middle bay, set with dishes, with the diners around it: one behind its west end, one at its east end and one hunched west of it; a round basin heaped with fruit or flowers stands in front of its east end (S3.prop.basin_16180).
entities.vis: part: legs behind the inner rail and the diners
entities.note: Top u 16100-16190, v 1377-1392 (seen as a thin plank under the heap); legs at about u 16125-16140 and 16180-16190 reaching v ~1405-1425 behind the inner rail. base = est middle of its feet. Dishes on its west half: S3.prop.dishes_16120. Scale: about 90 px long.

entities.name: tavern on the north bank at the bridge's north foot (虹桥边的小酒馆)
entities.what: An open-fronted tavern on the north bank just east of where the bridge comes down: a large roof with a lattice-filled gable at its east, a lower roof skirt with tile ends over a band of lattice windows, open bays on slender posts, and tables, benches and chairs under it at the water's edge; the bridge's tall end post with its crossed top stands at its west corner.
entities.vis: part: crossed by the big boat's lowered mast and lines (u 20100-20280, v 170-380); east end behind willow branches
entities.src: 名画记: 虹桥边的小酒馆 (pin 21)
entities.note: Roof: a long double line with hatching runs from the west eave corner (20056,120) up to the right through (20195,35) toward (20300,25); a gable at the east with its apex at ~(20300,25), its east slope down to (20375,105); inside the gable a row of vertical lattice bars, u 20245-20345, v 78-105. Below, a horizontal skirt with hatched tile ends at v 128-150 from u 20085 to 20390, and under it a lattice window band, u 20105-20230, v 150-200. Posts at u 20070-20075 (v 120-280), 20105-20110, 20215 (v 145-210), 20240-20245 (v 150-280), 20305-20320, 20375-20390 (v 100-280). Tables: one with a square top (20142-20207, v 220-244) and legs to v ~262-280; benches and chairs 20290-20380, v 190-280 (tiles' props, t9). Front base line est v ~285-290 (table feet); the boats' hulls start at v ~290-300 (river_e), so the tavern stands right at the water's edge. UPPER FLOOR? 刘涤宇 counts a two-storey building opposite 十千脚店 at the bridge. TWO READINGS: (a) one storey with a hip-and-gable roof: the lattice at v 78-105 is the gable's infill and the skirt at v 128-150 the main eave; (b) two storeys: an upper floor with lattice windows at v ~75-110 under the gable roof, and the skirt a pent roof over the ground floor. Under (b) the upper floor line is at about v 150 over u 20085-20390, straight above the ground at v ~288. The strokes at this resolution don't settle it; conf low for the storey count. The bridge's end post (crossed top at v 20-40, u 20040-20055) is the bridge agent's. Back corners est (placeholder, behind the lattice band). SCALE CUES (px): front ~325 wide; a table top ~65 x 24; posts ~165 px from skirt to floor. DEPTH DIRECTION: the table top's sides (20142,242)->(20160,220) and (20187,244)->(20207,220), slope -1.2 (table height, low-med); the roof's west eave line (20055,120)->(20195,35), slope -0.61 (high).

entities.name: long tiled building with an open front, south bank east of the bridge
entities.what: A long single-storey building along the south bank east of the big building: a big tiled roof (its ridge hidden under the hull of the boat moored at the bank) with a hipped west end, and an open front under the eave where people sit and stand at long tables and benches; plain wall panels and doors in the middle, a wall of vertical boards at its east end, and a pole from that end carries a hanging sack.
entities.vis: part: ridge under the moored boat's hull; front's foot behind the front building's roof (west) and a parasol stall (east); east end behind the big tree's trunk
entities.note: Roof tiles from v ~1195 (under the boat's hull) to the front eave at v 1443-1457, u 19685-20440; west end a hip (19650,1395)->(19750,1293)->(~19790,1200); east end hidden by the big tree (u 20410-20590). Open front: posts at u 19686, 19707-19717 (v 1430-1615), 19853-19880, 20016-20039 and 20053-20094 (plain light wall panels or doors, v 1465-1556), 20387-20444 (east end wall of vertical boards, v 1493-1590). Floor line: a horizontal beam at v 1607-1621 from u 19548 to 20000. Inside: a long table 19762-19850 (top v 1505, legs to v 1563-1565), a bench 19875-19920 (v 1505-1545), a low board or bench lying at 19792-19862 (v 1572-1612), a seated man at (19753-19775, 1440-1530), a standing man at (19853-19880, 1470-1552) (tiles' props and figures, t8/t9). A leaning framed board with small marks (a signboard? its writing unreadable: □□□□) at 19962-20007, v 1543-1588, standing on its own (t9's prop). East end: a pole at v ~1600-1610 from u 20340 to 20420 with a sack hanging from it (20380-20430, v 1590-1690): part of this building unless a tile reads it as a rack. WEST BAY (u 19548-19690): posts, a railing at v 1490-1530 and a diagonal plank from (19650,1530) to (19598,1615) (a stair?), under the big building's east eave; read as this building's open west bay (or a veranda on the big building's east side). A parasol stall stands in front of the east part on the ground at v ~1675-1714 (t9's props), so the ground in front is lower on the silk than the floor line: S3.road.south_street_20250. Back corners est (placeholder): 215 px of v behind the front, shifted along the west hip's slope. NOTE: the standing man inside is only 82 px tall at foot v 1552, against 160-190 px for figures on the open ground at v 1300-1700: this building's interior is painted at about half the near scale. SCALE CUES (px): eave to floor line ~165 px; front ~900 wide. DEPTH DIRECTION: the low board's sides (19792,1612)->(19817,1574) slope -1.52 and (19840,1612)->(19860,1574) slope -1.90 (ground level, med-low); west hip (19650,1395)->(19750,1293), slope -1.02 (high). Merge: t8 names two objects hung inside its west part at u 19620-19647, v 1453-1484 (hanging goods: part of this building), and plank or ladder lines at 19615-19685, v 1275-1441 west of its west hip, between it and S3.bld.mat_shed_19530 (unassigned: for the second pass). t9 reads its door posts at u 20014-20025, 20037-20060 and 20080-20095, the slatted panel at 20383-20458 (v 1497-1576) and the corner post at 20375-20383, as this note does. SECOND PASS (east): t8's unassigned 'plank or ladder lines at 19615-19685, v 1275-1441' belong to a planked sloping plane between the mat shed S3.bld.mat_shed_19530 and this building's west hip. The plane runs 19550-19775, v 1244-1375: boards run up to the east, parallel to the hip line (19650,1395)->(19790,1200), with a double-line edge on their west side. An upright post stands at u ~19560-19570 (v 1240-1330). The plane is bounded by the shed's front (west), the big hall's north bargeboard (south), the hip line (east), and the feet of S3.fig.parasol_capped_man_19652 under the tilted parasol (north). TWO READINGS, conf low: (a) this building's west hip face, drawn in boards rather than tiles (the hip face lies exactly here); (b) the board roof of a small lean-to between the shed and this building, which would need its own entity. Under either reading it is no ladder or loose plank, so no prop. Crops: p2e_c_shedeast_col.jpg, p2e_c_underarch_col.jpg, p2e_c_ladder_w.jpg, p2e_c_ladder_plain.jpg.

entities.what: Slender posts and two long horizontal beams just under the silk's top edge on the north bank, east of the shop: read as an open shed whose roof is off the silk; a porter with two baskets and other figures stand under it.

entities.note: Beams at v 23-27 (u 19550-19760) and v 55-58 (u 19550-19750); posts at u 19535-19540 (v 23-83), 19660 (v 23-57), 19693-19700. Figures under it (t8/t9's): a man at 19560-19640 (v 25-110), a porter with two baskets on a pole at 19640-19700 (v 30-128), a man at 19740-19800 (v 20-90). entities.name: building in front at the silk's bottom edge, south bank (roof only)
entities.what: A tiled roof at the silk's bottom edge in front of (south of) the long open shop: its top edge runs straight along the shop's floor line and its east end is a hip running down to the right; two posts show at its west end.
entities.vis: part: roof only; walls below the silk's bottom edge
entities.note: Top edge (read as its ridge or back eave) a straight double line at v 1607-1621 from u 19550 to 19993; tiles in rows below it to the silk's edge (v ~1775); east end a hip from (19993,1607) through (20150,1700) to (20290,1780); west end posts at u 19498-19507 (v 1634-1775) and 19535-19548 (v 1593-1693), with a diagonal brace. READINGS: a separate building in front of the open shop (its ridge touching the shop's floor line), or a pent roof over a lower storey of S3.bld.open_shop_20000; the parasol stall standing on the ground at v ~1700 just east of the hip, lower on the silk than the shop's floor line (v 1615), argues for a separate building with a street between them east of u 20000. Footprint is a placeholder below its roof (walls off the silk). SCALE CUES (px): ridge ~445 long. SECOND PASS (east): this closes t8's left-to item 'a building front with posts and a stair or ladder at 19330-19580, v 1660-1772', which was never assigned. The diagonal double band from (19506, 1774) to (19577, 1671) (slope about -1.45, the receding direction of the hall's eaves, -1.30) is this roof's west verge, seen running back. It is not a stair: no treads are drawn, only a few short marks. More upright posts with panels between them stand west of the posts named above: at u 19460-19470 and 19483-19493 (v ~1640-1770) and at 19507-19513. They are this building's west front, under the big hall's east eave, so its west end reaches u ~19460 rather than 19500 (placeholder footprint). Crops: p2e_c_bottomw_col.jpg, p2e_c_stair_col.jpg, p2e_c_stair_plain.jpg.

entities.name: mat-roofed shed with board walls, south bank under the arch's crown
entities.what: A low shed on the south bank under the arch: a single-pitch roof of cross-hatched woven mat sloping down to the front, over a front of vertical boards and door-like panels; a big parasol on its own pole stands in front of it and people crowd at its east end by the water.
entities.vis: part: wall feet hidden behind the big building's north bargeboard (v 1310-1390); roof crossed by a parasol
entities.note: Roof: back edge (19415,1140)->(19720,1145), front eave (19340,1235)->(19605,1215). Front wall: posts and vertical boards at u 19400, 19470, 19520-19530, 19555-19570, v 1240-1320; its foot is hidden behind the long curved bargeboard of S3.bld.bridge_foot_hall_19000's north gable, which passes (19294,1312) and (19550,1375). It is not a boat: no hull is drawn under it; the curved line below it is that bargeboard. A big parasol (19400-19630, v 1070-1125; pole at u 19510-19535 to v ~1205) and a second parasol (19650-19800, v 1180-1240) stand by it (tiles' props, t8); heads at 19600-19700, v 1080-1260 are people on the bank behind and beside it (t8's), or at the west end of the boat moored along the bank (river_e). The restyle turns it into a tiled shop with round basins (unusable here). SCALE CUES (px): roof ~380 wide, wall ~85 px tall.

entities.what: A shop on the north bank whose roof is cut off by the silk's top edge: only a band of lattice or boarded front shows under the edge, with tables and benches set out on the ground in front of it.
entities.vis: part: roof off the silk's top edge; only the lower front shows
entities.note: Vertical strokes (lattice or boards) at v 18-37 from u 19180 to 19400, a horizontal at v 37-40 (the front's foot or a sill); a post at u 19180-19183 (v 17-67). Tables and benches in front at v 60-97 (u 19190-19230, 19253-19307, 19297-19383; tiles' props, t7/t8) and a stall under a parasol at 19390-19480 (v 20-125). entities.name: mat-roofed shed on the south bank under the arch's south side

entities.vis: part: lower front behind the big building's north gable ornament and seated figures
entities.src: tile plan: the mat-awning stall under the arch (≈ 19000–19300)
entities.note: Mat roof u 19032-19320+, from its top edge (ridge) at v 1014 down to the front eave at v 1139-1145; west gable end a slanted mat flap from (19032,1014) down to (18986,1145); east end a mat panel at u 19300-19320 (v 1040-1200) and a post at u 19330-19340 (v 1140-1300). The bridge's tall south end post (u 19015-19027, v 850 to 1250+) stands just west of it (bridge's). Under the eave: seated men at tables, u 19080-19300, v 1140-1250 (t7's), a table top at 19155-19218, v 1190-1200 (t7's prop). The water's ripples reach v ~1010 just behind its ridge, so it stands on the bank's edge. Base est: front wall foot ~v 1290 (eave ~2 m above), back wall ~v 1200 (behind the ridge), back corners shifted +55 px of u along the receding slope; placeholder. t7's hint calls it a 'mat-awning stall': it has a gable roof on posts with people inside, so it is recorded here as a shed; t7 may also record it as a stall prop (a duplicate across kinds: drop one at merge). SCALE CUES (px): roof 290-345 wide; ridge to eave 125 px of v.

entities.name: tiled house behind the far-bank hall (roof only)
entities.what: A tiled roof behind (north of) the long hall, running off the silk's top edge, with a gable end and a post at its east end; its lower part is hidden behind the hall's roof and a stand of bare willow crowns.
entities.vis: part: roof only; lower part behind the hall's roof and willow crowns; top off the silk
entities.note: Tiles at u 18686-19014, v 18-86; its west edge a line from (18614,50) up to (18686,29); its top runs along the silk's top edge (v 16-20). East end: a small gable (two slanted lines) with a post at u 19021 (v 68-118) and a horizontal at v 105-114, at u 18990-19010. It could be the upper part of the hall's own roof (a hip running up to the right) rather than a second building: the line (18668,52)->(18855,105) between the two tile fields is read as the boundary between two roofs. SCALE CUES (px): visible roof ~330 wide.

entities.name: big gable-roofed building at the bridge's south foot (roof seen from above)
entities.what: The biggest roof on the south bank, at the bottom edge east of the bridge's south foot: an overhanging-gable (悬山) roof of round tiles seen from above, its ridge running back (north) from a south gable at the silk's edge to a north gable with a ridge-end ornament at the bridge's foot. The south gable is open: a log tie beam on four columns, a king post with a hanging-fish ornament and two small star-shaped ornaments, and two struts.
entities.vis: part: roof only; walls and ground below the silk's bottom edge or under the roof
entities.note: RIDGE: a straight double line from the south gable's apex (18861,1507) to the north gable's ridge-end ornament (19128,1155), slope -1.32. SOUTH GABLE: curved bargeboards from the apex, west through (18760,1640), (18640,1705), (18538,1748) to the silk's edge at ~(18505,1771); east through (19160,1717) to ~(19260,1790). Tie beam (a log) v 1670-1690 from u 18708 to 19003; king post with a hanging fish (悬鱼) at u 18861-18872, v 1544-1660; two star ornaments (惹草) at (18835,1600) and (18895,1600); columns at u 18708-18724, 18803-18814, 18914-18930, 19019-19035 from the beam (v ~1680) down past the silk's edge. A small figure stands inside the gable at (18819-18850, v 1723-1775) (t6's). NORTH GABLE: bargeboards from (19128,1155) west down to the NW eave corner (18595,1560) (curving: (19015,1255), (18840,1346), (18778,1380), (18677,1480)) and east through (19294,1312), (19550,1375) to the NE eave corner (19650,1400). EAVES: west eave (18418,1771)->(18580,1561), slope -1.30; east eave (19362,1775)->(19650,1400), slope -1.30; both parallel to the ridge. The SW and SE eave corners are just below the silk's edge (about (18450,1800) and (19330,1810)). entities.name: 十千脚店's riverside hall (two storeys, the upper floor with a railed balcony and diners)
entities.what: Long two-storey hall along the river bank, its front to the south: a big hip-gable (歇山) tiled roof, ridge with an ornament at its east end, a gable triangle with barge boards over the east end; under the eave a band of slanted slats and a beam; the upper storey's front of narrow bays between thin posts: lattice windows (15614-15681, 15861-15955, 15955-16028, 16211-16289), an open panel with a table (15681-15790), a doorway with a standing figure (15800-15855), and an open middle (16028-16197) where diners sit at a table with dishes and a small hanging cloth; in front a balcony with a railing of balusters, which turns at the south-east corner into a side gallery running back north-east under its own slatted roof (a figure stands in it). Under the balcony, east part only (15955-16300): a plain platform band and a tiled pent roof (腰檐) with drip tiles, i.e. the lower storey's eave. The lower storey's walls are not painted (bare trees and plain silk below the pent eave). No writing on it. At the back of the middle bay an open rack of shelves (u 16122-16160, v 1295-1337) stands beside the hanging cloth, a pot on it (S3.prop.pot_on_rack_16140); in the west doorway a plain partition panel (u 15837-15860, v 1320-1390) stands east of the doorway figure.

entities.src: 余辉: 欢楼美禄 (setting); sections.md:109 (刘涤宇: 十千脚店 two-storey)
entities.note: TWO STOREYS (tested, med conf): under the balcony railing there is no ground, step or column foot; directly below it are a beam (v 1508-1512), a plain platform band (1512-1548) and a tiled roof slope (top 1550-1556, tile ends 1645-1655, eave 1665-1670 with drip tiles), spanning only u 15955-16300 like the band. A roof under the floor = the floor is an upper floor (平坐 over a 腰檐). The alternative, a separate low building in front whose ridge happens to meet the band exactly and share its ends, is less likely. UPPER FLOOR: floor line (the balcony's bottom rail and floor beam) at v 1467-1487 over u 15750-16330, about 1455-1460 at 15600-15750 (behind branches); railing top rail v 1425-1430, window sills v ~1400; straight above the ground at v ~1770 est (hidden; a floor ~3.8 m up, (1770-1475)/77; the pent eave at 1668 fits a lower eave ~1.5 m below the floor projecting ~1.5 m). The side gallery's floor runs from (16330,1500) back to ~(16520,1350), its top rail from (16310,1440) to (16500,1280). TAVERN: read as 十千脚店's 楼 (upper floor of the tavern with drinkers at its windows): it is two-storey (刘涤宇 counts the tavern two-storey; no other two-storey building stands near the gate), its east gallery abuts S3.bld.tavern_wing_16300, and nothing painted (wall, lane, gap) separates it from the tavern's wing and gate. Conf med-low: a separate restaurant beside the tavern cannot be excluded. Roof: ridge (top edge) v 953-969 from its west end (15644, cut by S4b's willow crown) to the east ornament (16408,931); west hip (15644,960)->(15537,1200); front eave double line v 1222-1237; slat band under it v 1235-1290; beam v 1285-1300; east gable triangle 16340-16440 (v 935-1150), east hip (16408,935)->(16320,1262), east barge down-right to (16500,1137) over the gallery roof (16315-16520, v 1150-1250). SW corner post (15513-15540, v 1240-1470). Upper posts (bays above): 15592, 15607-15614, 15681, 15725, 15789-15800, 15861, 15908, 15955, 16028, 16097-16122, 16197-16211, 16289-16303; the bays list puts them on the est ground line. FOOTPRINT is a placeholder: front at the est ground under the balcony (v 1775), depth est 6 m (307 px of v), back corners shifted +294 px of u (dx 49, this area's measured receding slope ~-1.05: see the report's table). Its north side faces the river bank; the route is read along that bank behind it (S3.road.main). SCALE CUES (px): bays ~65-80 wide; lattice windows ~70 wide x 95 tall; seated diners ~100 px from head to seat (painted ~1.4x the frame's 77 px/m); railing 50 px (1427->1477); pent roof 112 px tall on screen. entities.name: the Rainbow Bridge (虹桥)
entities.what: A single-span arched timber bridge with no piers: its arch is a broad band of parallel curved timbers (the woven-beam arch, 编木拱) springing from both banks, and the deck rides on top of it, climbing from the south bank (picture lower left) over a high hump and coming down onto the north bank (upper right). Along the painted east (near) side runs a railing of X-braced panels between upright posts with a handrail; square beam ends stand out on the arch face, the biggest under the crown. The deck is packed with people and stalls; the big boat passes under the arch.

support_by.deck_c: bridge deck: 375 px west of the near edge
support_by.deck_w: bridge deck: 750 px west of the near edge

entities.vis: part: the south foot hidden behind the crowd at the south bank (v 1075-1290) and the big parasol (18660-18900, 880-1000); the north foot behind the big boat's mast lines (u 19950-20300, v 300-600); the west railing and the deck surface north of the crown hidden behind the crowd and the near railing
entities.src: 名画记: 虹桥 (pin 18); 名画记: 拥挤的桥面 (pin 20)
entities.note: LINES (scan px, west to east = south foot to north foot). deck_e = the painted east (near) edge of the deck, where the railing posts stand: the upper edge of the light outer beam of the arch (a band 16-20 px wide just under the railing), traced on the strokes every 2-3 px with a brightness profile across the band and checked on zoom-2/3 crops; points 18815-20000 measured, the end points est. Below the beam: a darker band of arch timbers, and the arch underside (arch_intrados_e) 60 px below deck_e on the flanks and 40 px at the crown (offsets checked on crops). deck_w = the west (far) edge: NOT PAINTED (hidden behind the crowd; no west railing is drawn). Estimated as deck_e shifted 750 px west at the same v (iso-height lines across this deck are level in the picture: see the bridge report). Evidence: where the deck crowd meets the water on the upstream side, its west boundary runs (18490, 395) -> (18300, 700), 700-800 px west of deck_e at the same v; north of the crown deck_w is behind the near railing and the arch (hidden). deck_c = the deck centre line (deck_e shifted 375 px west), est: the route's deck stretch for S3.road.main, leaving the south bank at (18435, 1090) and landing on the north bank at (19650, 396), the north half hidden behind the arch. FEET (base corners, ground H 0): se = deck_e's south foot, est (the edge is visible down to (18815, 1072), then hidden behind the heads of the people standing on the south bank, whose feet are at v ~1290; the foot is taken just below the last visible point; it could be up to ~200 px lower: see the report's alternatives). ne = deck_e's north foot at the foot of the near railing's capped end post (rail_end_n, a post with a pointed knob, top v 325, foot v ~396), where the deck edge flattens onto the north bank. sw and nw = deck_w's feet, est, at the same v as se and ne (sw among the shore-side stalls at the south bank, nw hidden behind the arch). Naming: the bridge runs south (lower left) to north (upper right); front = south; deck_e/deck_w replace the deck_s/deck_n named in the tile brief, because the deck's width lies across the picture (east-west), not up the silk. HEIGHTS (frame, 77 px/m): the deck profile [u, H] is in gen/map/S3/reports/bridge.md, H = (v of the ground line straight below - v of deck_e)/77, the ground line being the line through the two feet se and ne (the east face's foot on level ground: (18810, 1090) -> (20025, 396), slope -0.571). Highest deck H 5.44 m at u ~19330; the picture's highest deck point (19610, 280) is at H 4.65. support_by gives deck_e, deck_w and deck_c their own H profiles (bridge deck / bridge west edge / bridge centre line: the same heights at u, u-750 and u-375). NOT PAINTED / HIDDEN: the abutments and the arch's springings at the water (behind the south-bank crowd and behind the boat's mast lines at the north end); the west railing; the deck surface north of the crown. A woven arch needs abutments at both banks: parts of this entity, hidden. SCALE CUES (px): railing about 50 px from deck edge to handrail (rail_e_top, offset checked on crops), posts about 55-65 px apart on the south flank with an X-brace in each panel; outer deck beam 16-20 px; arch depth (deck edge to underside) 60 px on the flanks, 40 px at the crown; figures at the crown about 110 px from head to the deck edge; deck width (deck_e to deck_w) 750 px of u; deck_e from foot to foot 1215 px of u and 694 px of v. Beam ends: a framed block under the crown (u 19598-19645, v 300-332: a big transverse beam end, or a board; conf low) and a bracket-like block on the south flank (u 19104-19125, v 571-614). DEPTH DIRECTION: the foot-to-foot line se -> ne (18810, 1090) -> (20025, 396), slope -0.571, is the bridge's axis on the ground; the deck's cross direction is level in the picture. A square bridge (axis at right angles to the deck's width) needs a local receding direction of about dx 90 px/m here (51.25 / 0.571); with dx 31.6 (S4b's seam knot) the axis comes out 53 deg from east and the deck a parallelogram (report). Merge (the lead's note): the custom point list arch_intrados_e is now the line rib_e (same 16 points), because world() keeps lines and drops custom lists; the bridge kit takes its first and last points as the near-face springings at the water (support_by rib_e: water). Those two points are the ends of the traced intrados (18897, 1021) and (19977, 424); the springings themselves are hidden (behind the south-bank crowd, behind the mast lines), and the lead's study read them at about (18880, 1080) and (19960, 470). Merge: a short balustered railing piece IS painted at the deck's west edge, just west of t6's youth S3.fig.youth_round_face_18643: two diagonal rails with balusters rising east from rail_w_piece_s (18600, 432) to rail_w_piece_n (18640, 384) (t5: 18603-18639, v 374-426; t6: (18597, 393) to (18637, 443); merge crop gen/map/S3/look/merge_west_rail.jpg). Read as the last visible panel of the west (far) railing, conf low: it runs parallel to the near railing about 60-100 px east of the estimated deck_w at the same v, which supports deck_w to within that. Second pass: the 'west railing piece' (18593-18640, 384-462; the custom points rail_w_piece_s/_n added at the merge, now removed) is not the deck's west railing but S3.prop.slatted_panel_18615: it stands 590-670 px west of deck_e, 50-130 px inside the water's edge, with a seated man between it and the water, and it falls to the east while the railings rise to the east. It is no evidence for deck_w. The water's edge on the upstream side of the south ramp is 696-776 px west of deck_e at every v from 400 to 965 (mean ~725), which supports deck_w = deck_e - 750 to within ~25-50 px. Second pass (middle): the 35 `bridge deck` entities west of u 18810 stay on the deck: the line where the south ramp's crowd meets the water runs 696-776 px west of deck_e from v 400 to v 965 and follows the arch's curve, so it is the deck's far edge, not a bank. entities.name: 十千脚店's 彩楼欢门 (the festive pole scaffold over the gate)
entities.what: A towering openwork scaffold of lashed poles standing on the roof of 十千脚店's gate (S3.bld.tavern_gate_16870): a diamond-lattice band at its base, four horizontal tiers of cross-bars above it, and from them about eighteen poles rising: plain tall poles, three tapering spires of bound poles with many cross-ties, A-frames, and fans of poles splaying outward to the west and east like a crown. No flowers, streamers or lamp-boxes are hung on it (only lashings). The long bar from which the 新酒 banner hangs (t4's S3.prop.xinjiu_flagpole_17630) runs east from the scaffold's east side at v ~905: its west end is tied into the scaffold.

entities.note: SET PIECE. Stands on the gate roof, not on the ground: base corners are the gate's footprint (est); the custom pole points are where each pole's foot disappears (on the roof or into a tier) and its top. Heights above the est ground at the front (v 1795): lattice base v 1255-1320 (6.2-7.0 m), tiers at v 984-990 (1880-17274), 1040-1046 (16851-17315, the widest: the fans spring from its ends), 1072-1078 and 1116-1125 (16880-17315); the tallest top v 499 = 16.8 m on the front plane (the back poles stand further north, so less). POLES, west to east: pole1: top (16877,652), foot (16893,1255) - tall single pole at the west, slightly leaning west; foot est at the lattice base; pole2: top (16820,870), foot (16895,1040) - splays out west from the west end of tier 2; pole3: top (16808,943), foot (16870,1045) - splays out west, lower, from tier 2; pole4: top (16923,809), foot (16925,984) - A-frame of two legs (16910 and 16940 at tier 1) with a cross-tie at v 920; pole5: top (16942,759) - leaning west from the west spire; pole6: top (16945,856) - short leaning pole beside pole5; pole7: top (16976,659), foot (17000,956) - west spire: a tapering bundle of poles with many cross-ties, base 16958-17045 at v ~956; pole8: top (17015,532), foot (17035,1255) - second-tallest plain pole, rising out of the west spire; pole9: top (17055,711) - A-frame leaning east beside the west spire, a knob at its top; pole10: top (17087,622), foot (17110,980) - tall plain pole in the middle; pole11: top (17120,610) - middle spire with paired cross-ties; pole12: top (17166,606) - east spire with cross-ties; pole13: top (17200,697) - A-frame east of the east spire; pole14: top (17221,722) - short spire; pole15: top (17230,499), foot (17252,860) - the tallest pole, plain, with a wrapped joint at v 805-850; continues down behind the tiers; pole16: top (17280,795) - splays out east; pole17: top (17310,742), foot (17250,930) - splays out east from the east end of the tiers; pole18: top (17334,796) - splays out east, lowest of the east fan. Spires carry ties every ~25-35 px. The lattice band (16880-17113, v 1255-1320) is a parapet of diamond lattice panels; the east part of the base follows the gate's east eave up to ~(17330,1185). The 新酒 bar: v 900-912 from inside the scaffold (u ~17240-17300) east to its tip at u ~17585, just short of the pole at 17615; a stay runs from (17500,880) up to the pole. Pole tops +-5 px, feet est. East of the bridge's north foot (ramp foot ~(20030, 390)) the far bank recedes north: the bank's edge under the north-bank tavern's tables is at v ~288-295 (u 20150-20400), so the waterline is est just below it (v ~300-310), where the big boat's high stern and the north-bank boat (S2's) start (structures_e reads the boats' hulls from v ~290-300 there). shore_s: at u 18300 river_w's seam point (18300, 630, est). entities.name: far (north) bank under the hall on stilts, west of the bridge
entities.what: The river's far bank west of the bridge: a slope washed with dark ink streaks running down to the water under a long open hall whose floor stands out over it on posts.

entities.name: far (north) bank of the river, u 16150-18300
entities.what: The far bank: at 16150-16450 a wash-drawn earth slope rising north-east from the water to the path the five trackers climb; east of it a narrow strip of ground with bare trees and a willow, then shops with tables and stilted platforms along the top of the silk, the moored boats lying along its edge.
entities.vis: part: hidden behind the moored boats east of 16390
entities.note: bank_top = the ground's edge nearest the water. 16150-16450: the top of the wash band (bank slope 16150-16450, v 120-290; ink-wash patches only, no inked edge); the trackers' path climbs above it from (16330, 128) to (16430, 78) and off the top edge. 16450-17000: behind B3's cabin roof, est from the ground behind it (tree feet at v ~200-245, a row of rough strokes at 16600-16850 v 205-245 that may be stones or a low revetment). 17250-17650: the wash-drawn ground in front of the shops' tables (table legs at v 150-170) ends at v ~195-210. 18200-18330: the ground with a table and seated man (18270, 130) ends at the festooned line at v ~235-245. The far-bank hall on posts at 18330-18600 (structures_e) has its posts' feet at v ~245-265, at or in the water's edge. Never a vertical face: no stair or quay is drawn on this bank in u 15500-18300.

entities.name: far bank at the S4b seam, running off the silk's top edge
entities.what: The east end of the far (north) bank's strip that S4b paints along the silk's top edge: it continues S4b's far bank past the seam and leaves the silk at its top edge within about 150 px; a willow's whips hang over it from beyond the edge.
entities.vis: part: under the willow's whips; plain silk east of them
entities.note: FRAME (the cross-key seam check, asked for by the second pass west): S4b.grd.far_bank_15330 ends its bank_top and shore at u 15500 (est, hidden behind S4b's small cabin boat), and S3.water.bian_west_15500 had no shore_n west of (16150, 150): the water ran to the silk's top edge. On the scan, 15480-16150, v 0-150 is plain silk except the whips of S3.tree.willow_crown_top_15520 (no bank ink, no ripples), so the strokes cannot settle where the far bank leaves the silk. This entity is the shortest join: point 0 of each line is S4b's point at u 15500 (read from map/strokes/S4b.json each run), and both lines turn up off the silk's top edge by u 15600-15650, so the willow's est foot (15520, 70) stands on the bank. Other reading: the far bank runs on along the top edge to u ~16150 (then S3 would build a strip of far bank 650 px long). A question in map/frames/S3.json.

entities.name: near (south) bank of the river, u 15500-18300
entities.what: The south bank, never drawn as an edge: the riverside hall stands with its north eave at the water, reeds and bushes grow in front of it, then the tavern's bare trees, the 新酒 banner, the mat-roofed shed with the unloading boat moored along it, and the land at the bridge's south-west foot where the crowd stands at the water.

FRAME: point 0 is S4b.grd.near_bank_14850's bank_top at u 15500 (read from map/strokes/S4b.json each run; was (15500, 930, est), 15 px south).

entities.name: the Rainbow Bridge set piece
entities.what: The arched timber bridge with its three painted end posts (表木): two at its east corners and one on the far side of its south end: one set piece to build (the deck as a walkable surface, the railing, the woven arch, the posts).
entities.note: The people, stalls and parasols on the deck are the tiles' (t5-t9, support "bridge deck"); the boat under the arch and its crew are river_e's.

entities.name: the sedan and the horseman on the south ramp (车轿相争)
entities.src: 余辉: 车轿相争
entities.what: On the bridge's south ramp a sedan chair carried up by two bearers, with a man at its front pointing east up the bridge and two men in wide hats pointing back at it, meets a rider in white on a brown horse coming down westward from the crown: his groom hugs the horse's lowered neck to hold it, a man in front flings his arms wide, two men stand behind the horse, and a second horse's head shows behind the first.
entities.note: Joined at the merge from t6's S3.grp.sedan_party_18760 (the sedan's side) and t7's S3.grp.horseman_party (the horseman's side), both retired. Sedan side: S3.veh.sedan_18842 (no passenger painted), the bearers S3.fig.sedan_bearer_front_18838 and S3.fig.sedan_bearer_rear_18688, S3.fig.pointer_east_18830, and S3.fig.wide_hat_pointer_18855 and S3.fig.wide_hat_pointer_18890 (they point back at the sedan and may be the horseman's men, t6). Horseman side: S3.ani.horse_19055, S3.fig.rider_white_robe_19110 (seated, med), S3.fig.groom_holding_horse_19095, S3.fig.man_arms_flung_wide_18990 (low; may be one of the sedan's men), S3.fig.man_white_headcloth_19050, S3.fig.man_behind_rump_19165, S3.ani.second_horse_19230 (low: a second horse or a man in a dark head-cloth bent forward). Possibly in it but not joined: S3.fig.man_folded_arms_tall_cap_19270 (may ride the second horse, t7) and t7's S3.fig.man_dark_jacket_pointing_18915 and S3.fig.man_light_robe_reaching_18958 (in S3.grp.south_rail_watchers; may be on the sedan's side).

entities.name: the big boat and its crew (大船抢险)
entities.what: The big boat lowering its mast as it comes crosswise at the Rainbow Bridge, with its 19 crew recorded here: two men at the bow pointing the way, polers along the near gunwale, men on the far side pushing poles up at the arch and the cabin boat, men under the deckhouse, the stern hands hauling the mast's lines and a man in the cabin door with a long pole. People at the bridge's railings above (t7's and t8's) throw down a rope and shout (上下呼救); the men on the roof of the boat moored at the south bank (S3.grp.south_bank_boat_crew) wave and shout to it.
entities.src: 名画记: 大船穿行虹桥 (pin 19); 余辉: 大船抢险, 上下呼救
entities.note: 上下呼救 across groups: the rope thrower S3.fig.deck_youth_rope_19445 and the pole or rope holder S3.fig.deck_pole_holder_19625 (t8); the watchers and shouters at the near railing over the arch (t7: S3.fig.man_at_railing_face_west_19318 (t7's man facing us at the rail is t8's S3.fig.deck_rail_face_19350); t8: S3.fig.deck_rail_face_19350 to S3.fig.deck_stooping_hat_19765; t9: S3.fig.rail_watcher_19862, _19892, _19923); the wavers on the moored boat (S3.grp.south_bank_boat_crew). The merge may join them in one 上下呼救 group. Second pass (east): head_in_rigging_19990 (a rope hook under the rib) and boatman_stern_rail_20400 (the arms of S3.fig.boatman_stern_bending_20365) retired; 19 crew.

entities.name: the cabin boat under the arch and its two passengers
entities.what: A cabin boat under the bridge's arch with two men leaning on its railing, watching the big boat beside it.

entities.name: the boat moored at the south bank and the men on it
entities.what: The boat moored along the south bank east of the arch; two men on its roof wave and shout to the big boat at the bridge, one or two more look out of its hatch.
entities.src: 余辉: 上下呼救

entities.name: the boat under way and its crew
entities.what: Three men at the bow and five or six working the stern sweep of the boat under way (摇橹向前; the sixth, S3.fig.sweep_man_15888, is low).

entities.name: the towed boat, its crew and its five trackers

entities.note: Merge: t2's S3.grp.trackers_16380 (the five trackers) joined here and retired: one towing scene (名画记 pin 25 河边泊船 (纤夫) is pinned at u 15690, on the boat under way; the trackers stand at u 16325-16432).

entities.name: the long passenger boat

entities.name: the awning boat
entities.what: The boat with the fore awning, the boatman crouching under it (low) and the man seated in its cabin.

entities.name: the mat-cabin boat
entities.what: The boat with the dark mat cabin and its two seated passengers.

entities.name: the unloading boat and its porters

entities.name: 十千脚店 (the tavern complex)
entities.what: The tavern: its riverside two-storey hall with drinkers upstairs, the wing and the rear hall behind the gate, the gate with the 彩楼欢门 scaffold on its roof, the bar fence and the 十千脚店 lamp-box at its front, and the 杈子 barrier on the forecourt's west side.

entities.note: The riverside hall's membership is a reading (med-low); the rest belong together by the gate. The 新酒 pole and banner (t4), the rider at the gate (t3) and the big parasol east of the gate (t3) are tiles' entities.

entities.name: the diners on the riverside hall's balcony
entities.what: Three men eating and drinking at a long table in the middle bay of the riverside hall's railed balcony over the river road: one bearded in a dark cap behind the table, one hunched over the rail and a light-robed one standing at the back (host or waiter); a round basin heaped with fruit or flowers stands in front of the table, and a pot stands on the wall rack behind it.

entities.name: the pair at the hall's west doorway

entities.name: the jar and bottle stalls under the canopy

entities.note: The canopy over them is S3.prop.mat_canopy_17600.

entities.name: porters at the silk's bottom edge

entities.name: the open shed on the far bank

entities.name: the rider on the dark donkey

entities.name: the dark donkey on the ramp

entities.name: the twin parasols (饮子 stall?)

entities.note: The stall under them is hidden by the wall. The 饮子 identification is the pin's position (t5 reads it the same way), not a reading of the board.

entities.name: the mat-awning stall at the railing
